questions.statement: Which sentence correctly gives an opinion to start a discussion turn?
questions.context: Lucia wants to start her turn in a class debate about school uniforms.

options.text: In my view, uniforms save time.
options.feedback: Correct! In my view correctly opens a personal opinion politely, so it perfectly starts Lucia turn about school uniforms in a class debate.
The option Close the door is wrong because Close the door is an instruction about the classroom, which expresses no opinion and cannot open a debate turn.
The option What time is it is wrong because What time is it asks for information about time, which contributes no viewpoint to the uniform discussion.
The option I have a pen is wrong because I have a pen states possession of an object, which is irrelevant and offers no stance on uniforms.

questions.explanation: Giving opinions in discussion uses clear frames like In my view or From my perspective. These signals mark a personal stance politely and invite response. Memorizing two or three frames gives B2 speakers confident openings.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question best asks others for their opinions in a discussion?
questions.context: Diego wants to ask his classmates what they think about homework.

options.feedback: The option Do your homework now is wrong because Do your homework now is a command to act, which asks for no viewpoint and closes discussion.
The option Give me your pen is wrong because Give me your pen requests an object, which is unrelated to inviting classmates to share views.

options.text: What do you think about homework?
options.feedback: Correct! What do you think about homework correctly asks for viewpoints openly, so it perfectly invites classmates to share varied opinions in discussion.
The option The homework is long is wrong as an invitation because although it states one view, it does not ask others for their thoughts at all.

questions.explanation: Asking for opinions uses What do you think or How do you feel about. These open questions invite others to speak and keep discussion moving. Closed yes or no questions without opinion verbs are weaker for discussion.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Carmen wants to agree strongly. Which response fits best?
questions.context: Carmen agrees strongly with her friend about banning plastic bottles.

options.feedback: The option I totally disagree is wrong because I totally disagree expresses strong opposition, which contradicts Carmen wish to support the plastic bottle ban.
Correct! I totally agree with you correctly shows strong agreement, so it perfectly supports her friend proposal to ban plastic bottles at school.

options.text: I have no idea about it.
options.feedback: The option I have no idea is wrong because I have no idea admits lack of knowledge, which avoids taking any supportive stance in the discussion.
The option Change the topic now is wrong because Change the topic now refuses to engage, which blocks agreement and stops the discussion from progressing.

questions.explanation: Strong agreement uses I totally agree or You are absolutely right. These emphatic frames show full support and strengthen group consensus. Adding a reason after agreement makes the turn more persuasive and natural.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which reply disagrees politely and keeps the discussion respectful?
questions.context: Pablo must disagree politely with a classmate about late school start.

options.feedback: The option You are completely wrong is wrong because You are completely wrong attacks the speaker directly, which sounds rude and breaks polite discussion norms.
The option Shut up right now is wrong because Shut up right now is aggressive and silences the partner, which destroys respectful turn taking completely.

options.text: I see your point, but I disagree.
options.feedback: Correct! I see your point, but I disagree correctly softens opposition, so it politely contrasts views about late school start while respecting the classmate.
The option That is stupid nonsense is wrong because That is stupid nonsense insults the idea harshly, which offends the speaker and violates polite disagreement rules.

questions.explanation: Polite disagreement softens with I see your point, but or I am afraid I disagree because. Direct You are wrong sounds rude and breaks discussion flow. Softeners keep debate respectful while still showing contrast.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence interrupts a discussion politely and appropriately?
questions.context: Sara wants to interrupt kindly because she has an urgent point.

options.feedback: The option Stop talking at once is wrong because Stop talking at once orders the speaker to be silent, which is abrupt and violates polite interruption norms.

options.text: Sorry to interrupt, but may I add something?
options.feedback: Correct! Sorry to interrupt, but may I add something correctly apologizes and requests entry, so it kindly introduces an urgent point without offending.
The option You never let me speak is wrong because You never let me speak accuses the partner of selfishness, which creates conflict rather than polite entry.
The option I am leaving right now is wrong because I am leaving right now abandons the discussion entirely, which fails to introduce any point at all.

questions.explanation: Polite interruption uses Sorry to interrupt, but or May I add something here. Apology plus request protects the current speaker face. Bare interruptions like Listen to me sound abrupt and damage cooperation.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence hedges an opinion correctly and sounds cautious?
questions.context: Jorge is hedging his claim so he does not sound too absolute.

options.feedback: The option Everyone knows it is true is wrong because Everyone knows it is true claims absolute certainty, which is the opposite of careful hedging.

options.text: It seems that homework helps sometimes.
options.feedback: Correct! It seems that homework helps sometimes correctly hedges the claim, so it sounds cautious and thoughtful rather than absolute and dogmatic.

options.text: It is one hundred percent proven.
options.feedback: The option It is one hundred percent proven is wrong because It is one hundred percent proven asserts total certainty, which removes all caution from the statement.

options.text: No one can ever doubt it.
options.feedback: The option No one can ever doubt it is wrong because No one can ever doubt it forbids disagreement entirely, which clashes with the modest tone of hedging.

questions.explanation: Hedging softens claims with It seems, Perhaps, or In general. Hedges show caution and academic care, unlike absolutes like Everyone knows. B2 speakers use hedges to sound thoughtful rather than dogmatic.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Your partner says phones help learning. Which follow up keeps discussion alive?
questions.context: Elena must choose the best follow up question to keep talk going.

options.feedback: The option Anyway, what is for lunch is wrong because Anyway, what is for lunch abandons the topic abruptly, which kills the discussion instead of extending it.
Correct! Why do you think so correctly requests reasons and extends the turn, so it keeps the discussion moving while showing active listening.
The option Repeat that word again is wrong because Repeat that word again focuses on pronunciation only, which does not explore ideas or deepen the debate.
The option I must go right now is wrong because I must go right now ends participation immediately, which stops any further exchange of opinions.

questions.explanation: Good follow ups request reasons with Why do you think so or Can you give an example. They extend turns and show listening. Topic changes or bare repetitions stall discussion instead of deepening it.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which response best shows active listening in a discussion?
questions.context: Raul wants to show he is listening before giving his own view.

options.text: So you mean buses are too crowded?
options.feedback: Correct! So you mean buses are too crowded correctly paraphrases the partner, so it proves listening and checks meaning before Raul gives his own view.

options.text: I do not care at all.
options.feedback: The option I do not care at all is wrong because I do not care at all dismisses the partner message, which shows zero listening and blocks cooperative discussion.
The option Talk about something else is wrong because Talk about something else rejects the current idea, which ignores the speaker and changes direction rudely.
The option My idea is much better is wrong because My idea is much better jumps to self promotion, which skips acknowledgement and sounds arrogant in discussion.

questions.explanation: Active listening signals include nodding plus So you mean or If I understand correctly. Paraphrase proves attention and checks meaning before responding. Ignoring and jumping straight to self blocks cooperation.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence rejects an idea firmly yet politely? It concerns a class trip.
questions.context: Nora must reject an idea firmly but without insulting her partner.

options.feedback: The option Your idea is ridiculous is wrong because Your idea is ridiculous insults the proposal harshly, which offends the partner and breaks respectful debate.
The option You know nothing at all is wrong because You know nothing at all attacks personal knowledge, which is rude and irrelevant to the actual proposal.

options.text: I am not convinced because of the cost.
options.feedback: Correct! I am not convinced because of the cost correctly holds a firm stance politely, so it rejects the idea with a clear reason and without insult.
The option Whatever, do what you want is wrong because Whatever, do what you want surrenders without argument, which abandons discussion rather than rejecting with reasons.

questions.explanation: Firm but polite rejection uses I am not convinced because plus a reason. It holds ground while respecting the other speaker. Insults or silence either offend or fail to argue.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which phrase best manages turn taking when both speakers overlap?
questions.context: Iker and a friend both want the last word in a heated debate.

options.feedback: The option I will shout louder now is wrong because I will shout louder now tries to dominate by volume, which destroys fair turn taking and respectful listening.

options.text: Let us take turns so each can finish.
options.feedback: Correct! Let us take turns so each can finish correctly negotiates the floor fairly, so both speakers can complete ideas without shouting or overlap.
The option You must never speak again is wrong because You must never speak again bans the partner permanently, which ends discussion and violates equal participation.
The option I always speak the truth is wrong because I always speak the truth claims personal superiority, which does not solve the practical problem of overlapping turns.

questions.explanation: Turn taking phrases like After you or Let us take turns manage floor fairly. Explicit negotiation prevents shouting overlaps. Demanding the floor aggressively creates conflict and stops listening.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which spoken reason is strongest in a discussion about green spaces?
questions.context: Alba compares two ways of giving reasons in a spoken argument.

options.text: Parks help health because children play outside daily.
options.feedback: Correct! Parks help health because children play outside daily correctly links claim and concrete evidence, so it forms a strong spoken reason that persuades listeners.
The option Parks are good, trust me is wrong because Parks are good, trust me offers a slogan without evidence, which sounds weak and unconvincing in debate.
The option Parks, parks, parks forever is wrong because Parks, parks, parks forever merely repeats the noun, which provides no reason or supporting detail at all.
The option Everyone loves parks, bye is wrong because Everyone loves parks, bye asserts popularity and then exits, which avoids giving any real supporting reason.

questions.explanation: Strong spoken reasons link claim and evidence with Because and For example. Bare slogans without support sound weak. Because plus concrete detail persuades listeners and structures the turn clearly for B2 discussion.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Replace the rude reply with the most polite alternative that keeps the meaning.
questions.context: Hugo hears a rude reply and must replace it with a polite alternative.

options.feedback: The option What nonsense are you saying is wrong because What nonsense are you saying mocks the partner contribution, which is rude and blocks respectful exchange.
The option You are talking rubbish now is wrong because You are talking rubbish now insults the speaker content, which offends and escalates conflict in discussion.

options.text: Could you clarify what you mean?
options.feedback: Correct! Could you clarify what you mean correctly requests explanation politely, so it repairs the rude reply while keeping the wish to understand the idea.
The option Nobody cares about that is wrong because Nobody cares about that dismisses the idea as worthless, which silences the partner and ends cooperation.

questions.explanation: Polite alternatives replace commands with requests and insults with I language. Could you clarify replaces What nonsense. Rephrasing keeps meaning but repairs tone, a key discussion repair skill.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence concedes a point gracefully and then defends the main view?
questions.context: Leire must concede a small point before defending her main idea.

options.text: You are totally wrong about all.
options.feedback: The option You are totally wrong about all is wrong because You are totally wrong about all denies everything, which misses the chance to concede a valid small point gracefully.

options.text: I give up on everything now.
options.feedback: The option I give up on everything now is wrong because I give up on everything now surrenders the whole argument, which abandons the main idea instead of defending it.

options.text: You are right about cost, however quality matters.
options.feedback: Correct! You are right about cost, however quality matters correctly concedes one point then pivots, so it builds credibility while still defending the main idea.
The option Cost never matters at all is wrong because Cost never matters at all denies an obvious fact, which sounds unreasonable and weakens the speaker credibility.

questions.explanation: Concession structures like You are right about cost, however quality matters admit truth then pivot. They build credibility before countering. Total surrender or total denial both miss the partial agreement move.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which invitation best includes a quiet student in the discussion?
questions.context: Mario wants to invite a quiet classmate to join the debate.

options.text: Speak now or stay silent forever.
options.feedback: The option Speak now or stay silent forever is wrong because Speak now or stay silent forever threatens the quiet student, which raises anxiety and discourages participation.

options.text: We have not heard from you yet, Ana, what do you think?
options.feedback: The option Ana agrees with me, right is wrong because Ana agrees with me, right speaks for Ana and pressures agreement, which denies her a genuine voice.
Correct! We have not heard from you yet, Ana, what do you think correctly names and invites gently, so the quiet classmate feels welcomed to join safely.

options.text: Let the best students talk only.
options.feedback: The option Let the best students talk only is wrong because Let the best students talk only excludes quieter voices explicitly, which contradicts inclusive invitation completely.

questions.explanation: Inviting quiet speakers uses We have not heard from you yet or What is your view, Ana. Naming plus open question lowers pressure. Speaking for them or ordering them to talk increases anxiety.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best closes a turn and passes the floor politely?
questions.context: Clara must end her discussion turn and hand the floor to the next speaker.

options.text: I stop here and say nothing.
options.feedback: The option I stop here and say nothing is wrong because I stop here and say nothing ends abruptly without handover, which leaves the next speaker unsure when to start.

options.text: I am tired of this topic.
options.feedback: The option I am tired of this topic is wrong because I am tired of this topic complains about boredom, which closes negatively rather than handing over positively.

options.text: That is my view on clubs, what about you?
options.feedback: Correct! That is my view on clubs, what about you correctly summarizes and invites the next speaker, so it hands the floor clearly and keeps flow.
The option This topic is finished forever is wrong because This topic is finished forever declares the debate closed for all, which denies others their turn to speak.

questions.explanation: Closing a turn uses That is my view, what about you or Over to you. Explicit handover avoids awkward silence and shows control. Simply stopping or walking away leaves the floor unclear.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which reply most constructively builds on a weak idea about school trips?
questions.context: Adrian must pick the most constructive response to a weak argument.

options.feedback: The option That idea is totally useless is wrong because That idea is totally useless attacks without offering help, which discourages the speaker and stalls collaborative progress.

options.text: Nice idea, let us talk football.
options.feedback: Correct! That is a good start, and we could also consider cost correctly validates effort then adds a dimension, so it constructively improves the weak argument.

options.text: That is a good start, and we could also consider cost.
options.feedback: The option Nice idea, let us talk football is wrong because Nice idea, let us talk football praises then abandons the topic, which wastes the chance to strengthen the argument.
The option I already knew all that is wrong because I already knew all that boasts about self knowledge, which ignores the proposal and adds no useful extension.

questions.explanation: Constructive feedback adds ideas with That is a good start, plus we could also consider. It validates effort then extends. Pure praise without addition or pure attack without help both stall progress.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which phrasing fits a formal panel discussion about exams best?
questions.context: Aitor compares formal and informal ways to state views in a panel.

options.feedback: The option I dunno, exams stink is wrong because I dunno, exams stink uses slang and vague complaint, which sounds careless and weak in a formal panel.

options.text: From my perspective, exams cause stress.
options.feedback: Correct! From my perspective, exams cause stress correctly uses formal framing, so it suits a panel with teachers and shows respectful academic register.
The option Stuff about exams rules is wrong because Stuff about exams rules is vague slang without structure, which fails to convey a clear formal position.
The option Yeah, whatever, exams whatever is wrong because Yeah, whatever, exams whatever signals indifference with filler, which undermines credibility in formal discussion.

questions.explanation: Formal discussion prefers From my perspective and The evidence suggests over slang like I dunno, stuff rules. Register matching shows awareness of audience. Slang in a formal panel sounds careless and weakens authority.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which summary fairly reports group opinions before voting on school hours?
questions.context: Nerea must summarize group views fairly before the class vote.

options.text: We all agree with my idea.
options.feedback: The option We all agree with my idea is wrong because We all agree with my idea falsely claims unanimity, which hides dissent and distorts the group position.
The option Only smart people support libraries is wrong because Only smart people support libraries insults opponents as ignorant, which is biased and unfair to other views.
The option Forget the vote, I decide is wrong because Forget the vote, I decide seizes control autocratically, which cancels democratic discussion and fair summary.

options.text: Some of us support late start while others prefer early.
options.feedback: Correct! Some of us support late start while others prefer early correctly reports both sides neutrally, so it fairly summarizes views before the class vote.

questions.explanation: Fair summaries report both sides with Some of us think while others feel. They avoid bias toward personal preference. One sided summaries distort the vote and break trust in discussion leadership.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence best brings the discussion back to recycling politely?
questions.context: Unai faces a partner who keeps changing the subject away from recycling.

options.feedback: The option You always avoid the truth is wrong because You always avoid the truth accuses the partner of dishonesty, which creates conflict rather than calmly refocusing the talk.

options.text: Fine, let us talk about games.
options.feedback: The option Fine, let us talk about games is wrong because Fine, let us talk about games surrenders to the tangent, which abandons recycling and loses discussion focus.
The option Stop talking forever, please is wrong because Stop talking forever, please silences the partner completely, which ends cooperation and solves no focus problem.

options.text: Let us return to recycling since time is short.
options.feedback: Correct! Let us return to recycling since time is short correctly names the topic with a practical reason, so it politely refocuses discussion without accusing anyone.

questions.explanation: Redirecting politely uses Let us return to recycling because time is short. It names the topic and gives a practical reason. Accusing the partner of evasion or following every tangent both lose focus and control.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which mediator line best handles strong disagreement in a panel discussion?
questions.context: Ane leads a difficult panel where two speakers strongly disagree.

options.text: You are right and you are wrong.
options.feedback: The option You are right and you are wrong is wrong because You are right and you are wrong takes sides openly, which violates neutral mediation and inflames the losing speaker.

options.text: You both raise valid concerns, so let us compare evidence.
options.feedback: The option Stop arguing and be quiet is wrong because Stop arguing and be quiet shuts debate by command, which suppresses ideas instead of guiding evidence based comparison.
The option My view is the only correct one is wrong because My view is the only correct one imposes the mediator personal stance, which abandons facilitation for domination.

options.text: My view is the only correct one.
options.feedback: Correct! You both raise valid concerns, so let us compare evidence correctly validates both speakers then proposes criteria, which mediates disagreement productively and fairly.

questions.explanation: Mediating disagreement uses You both raise valid concerns, so let us compare evidence. It validates both sides then proposes criteria. Taking sides or shutting debate down fails the mediator role in panel discussion.
questions.subject: ingles
